meta.note: Things an executive should notice. level: risk = could slow or block demand; opportunity = a clear opening; caution = limit of the data. scope is a state code or US. Every item cites sources; Inferred means it rests on a secondary report or on reasoning.

items.title: Chip tax credit deadline
items.text: The 35% investment tax credit applies only to fabs that begin construction before Dec 31, 2026; Congress is weighing an extension. Fab timing could shift either way.

items.title: EV slowdown
items.text: Battery plants were cancelled, idled or restructured in 2025-26 (KORE in Arizona, Ultium Warren in Ohio, BlueOval SK split). Demand may lean to energy-storage cells.

items.title: ThermGAS DMC spec conflict
items.text: ThermGAS shows 0.5 ppm on its battery page and 1 ppm in its DMC application note. DMC is also missing from its Master Gas List. Publish one tested number before comparing with rivals.

items.title: Honeywell product status unclear
items.text: Honeywell's U.S. pages mark Li-ion Tamer Gen 3 as Discontinued, but its Gen 3 data sheet and gigafactory page are current. Do not claim anything about its status until Honeywell confirms.

items.title: No U.S. battery reference
items.text: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant DMC case study. The first credible reference site would stand out.

items.title: Lamp life: 4 months
items.text: ION Science's FALCO 2 11.7 eV lamp lasts up to about 4 months (3-month lamp warranty), and a PID responds to every solvent in the room. This is the clearest documented weakness to test against.

items.title: Announced, not spent
items.text: Data center dollars are announced investment from a secondary tracker (compiled Apr-Oct 2026). Some projects will be cancelled or resized. Counts of projects under construction are the safer signal.

items.title: Plants, not buyers
items.text: Pharma counts are Census establishments with paid employees, not sites that need leak detection. County detail covers 1,324 of 1,854 plants because the Census hides small-county detail.

items.title: Tax exemption being repealed
items.text: HB 463 (2026), as passed, repeals the sales and use tax exemption for data center equipment, applicable to tax years from Jan 1, 2026. The signing date was not confirmed. New starts may slow.
items.status: Verified (bill text); signing date not confirmed

items.title: Hyundai-LG plant start unconfirmed
items.text: The HL-GA plant's opening was delayed by the Sept 2025 immigration raid; April 2026 reporting says it was about to open. A production start was not confirmed. FREYR Newnan is reported cancelled by a secondary tracker.

items.title: Home state
items.text: ThermGAS is headquartered in Roswell, GA, so service and site visits are closest here. 43 data center projects and 3 battery plants are in the state.

items.title: New tax exemptions paused
items.text: On May 27, 2026 the Governor told the Tax Credit Authority to pause new data center exemption requests while a legislative committee studies growth. Already-exempt data centers reported $27.2B of capital investment in 2025. It is not a ban.

items.title: Ultium Warren idle
items.text: The Warren plant has been idle since January 2026, with a partial restart planned later in 2026.

items.title: New electricity tax, exemption under study
items.text: From July 2026 to July 2028 data centers pay $0.011/kWh on electricity consumed, and the 2026 budget orders a study of the sales-tax exemption. The incentive regime is in flux.

items.title: Most projects under construction
items.text: 58 projects, 26 already under construction, plus a state sales-tax exemption of up to 20 years for large projects (at least $500M and 40 jobs).

items.title: Samsung Taylor status
items.text: Samsung's Taylor fab start slipped from 2024 to 2025; its current operating status was not confirmed from a primary source.

items.title: BlueOval SK split
items.text: Ford and SK On dissolved their joint venture in Dec 2025; Ford takes the Kentucky plants and the second Kentucky plant was postponed. AESC Bowling Green is reported paused by a secondary tracker.

items.title: Ownership change at Stanton
items.text: SK On is to own and operate the Tennessee plant after the Ford JV split, and its focus is shifting toward stationary storage.

items.title: KORE plant cancelled
items.text: KORE Power cancelled its roughly $1B Buckeye plant in Feb 2025. LG Energy Solution's Queen Creek start (targeted for H1 2026) was not confirmed.

items.title: Micron New York delayed
items.text: Micron moved the opening of its first Clay, NY fab from 2028 to Q3 2030, so construction-stage demand there is later than first announced.

items.title: Micron Idaho timing
items.text: First wafer output is reported for mid-to-2H 2027 by trade press; no company release was read in full.

items.title: Panasonic producing
items.text: Panasonic's $4B De Soto plant opened in July 2025 and is in mass production, with a second wing under way.

items.title: Toyota producing
items.text: Toyota's $13.9B Liberty plant began shipping in June 2025 with an official launch in Nov 2025; more lines are scheduled through 2030.

items.title: DMC producer plant
items.text: UBE's integrated DMC/EMC plant (100,000 t/y of DMC) is a large-volume DMC handler outside cell making. Completion was planned for July 2026; start-up status was not confirmed.

items.title: Plant status not re-checked
items.text: Michigan has three plants and high model rank, but none of their 2025-26 statuses was re-verified in this research.

items.title: Possible double count
items.text: The tracker lists two Homer City rows of $10B each that may be the same campus. Counting it once gives $74.0B announced instead of $84.0B.

items.title: Planning regions, not counties
items.text: Connecticut's Census data now uses planning regions that the county map cannot draw; those rows appear in the list but not on the map.
